Question: How is convolution represented in the frequency domain?
Evidence:
[E1] (text, Section 3.2, page 4): To reduce the number of required operations when evaluating convolutional layers, we use the Convolution Theorem : the convolutions in the space domain are equivalent to pointwise products in the frequency domain. Denoting F − 1 as the inverse FFT, the convolutions between inputs x and y can be computed as follows:
[E2] (text, Section 3.2, page 4): This transformation can be used to accelerate training and prediction of CNN models. The basic idea is to convert the input and ﬁlters of a convolutional layer to the frequency domain, and then perform the pointwise product instead of the convolution. In this paper, we use the similar idea to speed up the convolution operation in the ciphertext domain, and we will show that FFT operations have little effect on the performance of a CNN model.
[E3] (text, Section 3.2, page 3): In image processing, the well-known fast Fourier Transform (FFT) is an algorithm that can convert an image from its space domain to a representation in the frequency domain and vice versa [36]. claims.text: Convolution in the frequency domain is represented as a pointwise product.
